FCDI.name: Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
FCDI.source: Flow-Electrode Charge Transport Studies (Rommerskirchen et al.)

EDI.name: Electrodeionization
EDI.source: DuPont EDI-310 Vendor Technical Specification & ASTM Standards

CDI.name: Capacitive Deionization
CDI.flowConfiguration: Cyclic batch or continuous single-pass through planar porous electrode gap
CDI.electrodeConfiguration: Fixed porous carbon electrodes (activated carbon cloth/film) on metallic current collectors
CDI.ionTransport: Non-Faradaic electrostatic adsorption into Electrical Double Layers (EDLs)
CDI.polarity: Cyclic DC voltage (0.8–1.5 V charging / adsorption; 0 V or short-circuit discharge / desorption)
CDI.productStream: Desalinated product water produced during adsorption cycle
CDI.concentrateStream: Concentrated brine waste produced during electrical discharge/desorption cycle
CDI.pretreatment: 5 µm cartridge filter, anti-scalant if hardness exceeds 200 mg/L as CaCO3
CDI.regenerationMode: Intermittent electrical short-circuiting or reverse voltage discharge
advantages: Low electrical energy consumption for low-salinity feed
Low initial capital expenditure without ion-exchange membranes
Simple cell construction and straightforward operational control
limitations: Subject to co-ion expulsion loss, reducing charge efficiency (~82%)
Lower water recovery (~90%) compared to membrane-enhanced systems
Unsuitable for high feed salinity (> 1,000 mg/L TDS)

MCDI.name: Membrane Capacitive Deionization
MCDI.flowConfiguration: Cyclic batch or continuous single-pass through membrane-bounded flow channel
MCDI.electrodeConfiguration: Fixed porous carbon electrodes with attached AEM and CEM sheets
MCDI.membraneConfiguration: AEM (Anion Exchange Membrane) at Anode; CEM (Cation Exchange Membrane) at Cathode
MCDI.ionTransport: Electromigration through ion-selective membranes into porous carbon EDLs with co-ion blocking
MCDI.polarity: Cyclic DC voltage (1.0–1.6 V charging / adsorption; 0 V or reverse -0.2 to -0.6 V discharge)
MCDI.productStream: High-purity desalinated product water produced during adsorption cycle
MCDI.concentrateStream: Concentrated brine waste produced during electrical discharge/desorption cycle
MCDI.pretreatment: 5 µm cartridge filter, turbidity < 1 NTU, anti-scalant for hard feed water
MCDI.regenerationMode: Intermittent electrical discharge / reverse polarity discharge with membrane co-ion blocking
advantages: Ion-exchange membranes block co-ion expulsion, boosting charge efficiency (~92%)
Higher salt removal rate (up to 94%) and higher water recovery (~95%)
Faster desorption flush with reversed polarity operation
limitations: Higher capital cost due to ion-exchange membrane sheets
Potential risk of organic or scaling membrane fouling under hard water

FCDI.name: Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
FCDI.flowConfiguration: Continuous dual-loop flow: feed water in central channel, carbon slurry circulating in anode/cathode channels
FCDI.electrodeConfiguration: Flowing carbon slurry micro-electrodes (5–20 wt% activated carbon suspension) with graphite current collectors
FCDI.membraneConfiguration: AEM at Anode slurry channel; CEM at Cathode slurry channel separating slurry from water channel
FCDI.ionTransport: Continuous electromigration across AEM/CEM into mobile carbon slurry micro-particles
FCDI.polarity: Continuous DC voltage (1.0–1.8 V across flowing slurry micro-electrode channels)
FCDI.concentrateStream: Continuous concentrated brine stream / regenerated slurry stream from un-charging reservoir
FCDI.pretreatment: Multi-media filter, viscosity conditioning, 10 µm pre-filter for slurry protection
FCDI.regenerationMode: Continuous external slurry un-charging in slurry reservoir tank or secondary un-charging cell
advantages: Continuous desalination operation without batch adsorption/desorption pause cycles
High salt sorption capacity via continuously circulating carbon slurry electrodes
Capable of treating high-salinity feed water (1,000 to 15,000+ mg/L TDS)
limitations: Complex slurry circulation loops, hose pumps, and regeneration infrastructure
Higher parasitic pumping energy for viscous slurry flow

EDI.name: Electrodeionization
EDI.flowConfiguration: Continuous dual stream: Feed split into Diluate (Product) channels and Concentrate (Reject) channels
EDI.electrodeConfiguration: Solid dimensionally stable anode (Ti/Pt or IrO2) and cathode (Stainless Steel) terminal plates
EDI.membraneConfiguration: Alternating AEM and CEM sheets forming Diluate and Concentrate compartments filled with mixed-bed resin
EDI.ionTransport: Electric field electromigration via conductive mixed-bed resin beads and ion-exchange membranes
EDI.polarity: Continuous DC high voltage (1.0–6.0 V per cell pair; constant polarization electric field)
EDI.productStream: Continuous ultrapure product water (< 0.05 mg/L TDS; > 16.0–18.2 MΩ·cm resistivity)
EDI.concentrateStream: Continuous concentrate reject stream carrying migrated ions (recirculated or wasted)
EDI.pretreatment: MANDATORY RO Permeate feed (TDS < 30 mg/L, Hardness < 0.5 mg/L as CaCO3, Silica < 0.5 mg/L)
EDI.regenerationMode: Continuous in-situ electrochemical water splitting (H2O -> H+ + OH-) — Chemical-free continuous operation
advantages: Produces ultra-pure water (< 0.05 mg/L TDS / up to 18.2 MΩ·cm)
Continuous electrochemical resin auto-regeneration via water splitting (H+ / OH-)
limitations: Requires low TDS feed (< 30 mg/L TDS / RO permeate) & hardness <= 0.5 ppm as CaCO3
Direct raw feed operation is not feasible without upstream feed conditioning
